Messages.Author: hamdamcwa
Messages.Body:
I feel a little embarressed asking this, but one of my players last
night would not accept what I was saying about this:

Talaq the Immortal. Unique Mage with 3 life, 1R damage, 0 bleed.

Talaq may play cards that require basic Quietus or basic Thaumaturgy
as a vampire with a capacity of 3. Any cost in blood is paid with his
life. If a card would give him blood, give him life. Talaq gets an
optional maneuver each combat.

Can he play Foul Blood?

Foul Blood, Qui, 1 Blood

BAS:Only usable when a vampire controlled by another Methuselah
successfully hunts.

That vampire gains one less blood from the blood bank and takes 1
damage (damage not preventable). Tap this reacting vampire.

SUP: As above, but this reacting vampire does not tap.

The question comes because the player in question noticed the text on
Foul Blood that says "tap this reacting vampire". He also noticed that
Talaq was an ally, not a vampire.

Answers?

Regards

DH

I'm pretty sure he can.

An old reference:

From: LSJ (vte...@white-wolf.com)
Subject: Re: Some thoughts, Annotated Rulesbook [was: Ex Nihiled Mummies]
View: Complete Thread (47 articles)
Original Format
Newsgroups: rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
Date: 2001-07-29 14:54:00 PST

> Can Ghouled Street Thug "use" Torn Sign Post?

He can play it, yes.

> Can Talaq the Immortal "use" Shot Gun Ritual ?

He can play it, yes.

> Can Talaq the Immortal "use" (and tap by it) Foul Blood ?

He can play it, yes.

> Can Talaq the Immortal "use" Veil of Silence ?

He can play it, yes.

> Can Kherebutu "use" a Soul Stealing ?

He can play it, yes.

Also note that there has been a change to how allies play discipline cards
(though I don't think it changes the answer to your question).

"Some allies have the ability to play certain cards "as a vampire." In these
cases, the ally is treated as a vampire for all effects generated by the play
of the card. The ally’s life represents his blood (to pay costs, for
example). Any blood he gains or loses as a vampire equates to a gain or loss of
life for the ally. For purposes of that card, the ally has a capacity of 1 by
default (for use if the card requires an older vampire or a vampire of a given
capacity). The ally is treated as a vampire only when playing the card and, for
cards such as actions and strikes that are not resolved immediately, for the
resolution of the effect. In particular, the ally is not treated as a vampire
for effects of the card once it's in play or for lingering effects generated by
the card. If the ally gains life in excess of his capacity, it doesn't drain
off, and if the effect inflicts aggravated damage on the ally, he burns life as
normal. However, if the effect would send the ally to torpor, then he is burned
instead."

Foul Blood is not an action or combat card that resolves later on, nor does it
have any special lingering effects. It is resolved immediately so Talaq is
"treated as a vampire for all effects generated by the play of the card." Thus
explaining the interaction with "tap this reacting vampire." There! =)

Halcyan 2

> Correct. It is a card that requires basic Quietus. QED.

Sorry LSJ I have to correct you here. The use of QED in this situation is
not appropriate. QED is the final word on a formal proof but a formal proof
has to start with an assumption and the conditions followed by a
mathematical/logical proof.

Just joking a little. :-) I was hoping that I could say that to somebody
since I got my first math test at university back (years ago) with 0 points
and more or less this sentence written on it in red ink :-).
